content.value: THE HEAD-BURNS-TICKET DEFECT IS CONFIRMED BY CONTENT, NOT YET BY EXECUTION. Full trace on the composed tree: refuse_head_on_side_effecting_gets runs at router.ex:303 with side_effecting_get?/1 fencing exactly two oauth paths plus a catch-all false (router.ex:479-489), so [v1, events] falls through; Plug.Head at router.ex:305 rewrites the method to GET and stashes nothing; the get /v1/events handler calls require_user_sse, which falls through to conn.query_params[ticket] and then Accounts.consume_sse_ticket(ticket); and consume_sse_ticket/1 (accounts.ex:2047) takes a bare binary, locks FOR UPDATE and stamps revoked_at unconditionally, structurally incapable of knowing the HTTP method. No HEAD test against /v1/events exists in either slice's test file - every HEAD test in router_sse_ticket_test.exs targets the mint route. The defect was invisible to both builders because each was inside its own fence. Adding side_effecting_get?([v1, events]) is sufficient AND architecturally correct: the plug is unconditional, runs before Plug.Head (so it still sees the true method) and before route dispatch, and matches path segments only. Threading a conn into Accounts would break the layering both slices otherwise preserve.

content.value: THE CSS CLASS IS SMALLER THAN THE DIRECTION THOUGHT, AND THE CHEAP FIX MAY NOT LIVE IN __css_check AT ALL. There are FOUR setAttribute data-* sites in app.js, not three: :3312 data-theme, :3344 data-bp-theme, :11871 data-state, and :16178 data-theme inside coherenceStampTheme - a second theme emitter the direction's recon missed. Both are cheap; the choice is real and should be made with a run, not a preference.

content.value: THE TRIPWIRE IS THE WAVE'S ONLY GENUINELY HARD SLICE, AND THE DIRECTION UNDERSOLD IT. There is NO first-party Elixir AST precedent anywhere in cloud/ (Code.string_to_quoted and Macro.prewalk hit only deps/) and no .credo.exs to hang a custom check on. content.value: THE ORACLE COLLISION IS REAL BUT NARROW, AND IT HAS A ONE-LINE REMEDY. Only ONE leg of one scenario is at risk: cch-w2-revoke-ux-honesty's AC2 gates a confirmModal on revoke-all only; per-row Revoke gets a toast plus a pending state and its DELETE still fires on the same click. At DESTROY tier the oracle must also set the typed-echo field and dispatch input, materially more. Two hazards Decide must fence: (a) a harness FIDELITY GAP - openModal replaces the modal body wholesale in a real browser, but the shim's flat parser only recognises button and a tags and #sessions-box is an independent registry singleton, so a post-confirm session-list assertion can pass in the shim while the real browser shows a closed modal, unless onConfirm re-renders the way app.js:975 does; and (b) none of the ux-honesty ACs say edit account-modal-revoke IN PLACE, do not duplicate, so a builder could leave the existing scenario permanently red on merge.

The grade: A-

GENUINELY STRONG. The wave did what its own frame demands and did it to itself. Four filed criteria were refuted by measurement and rewritten rather than built, and the builders kept doing it: slice 1 found that this charter's D34 wrapper list does not reproduce its own numbers (the 8 named wrappers give 40/5/17, not 45/5/12) and filed a correction row instead of quietly patching the classifier; slice 4 found a FOURTH open patch sibling in self-review after D52 named three; slice 3 re-measured the attribute population and found FIVE where the brief said four. Every builder's own review section reads like an adversary's, naming the judgement calls (the :sync exemption, the counts-not-sets pin, the unmeasured theft-by-overwrite hole) instead of burying them. The proofs are mutation-killed in both directions, not merely green. Seven follow-up rows were filed published mid-build. That is the epic's predicate turned on the epic, sustained across six independent agents.

WHAT FALLS SHORT, and why it is a minus rather than a plus. Three separate stale-source-citation defects shipped in one wave — one slice pinned line numbers its own sibling invalidated, one refreshed four citations and left six, and one pre-existing citation had already rotted. That is D41's disease, in the wave that MINTED D41, and no builder caught it because each looked only at its own file. It cost the reviewer three fixes and earned a new row. Second, the census pin is counts and not sets, so a same-commit class swap passes — defensible under bp-honest-gates D5/D11 and now stated outright, but a real hole in a slice sold as a drift ceiling. Third, the wave's own residual harms are named and unclosed by construction: claim theft-by-OVERWRITE was filed with 'MEASURE FIRST' as its first criterion because the builder honestly did not run the probe, and the forged-fresh-create -> Tasks.Queue.ready hole has no compensating control. Fourth, one slice (css-check boundary) is 63 lines of comment that changes no gate behaviour — correct per D49, and the builder said so plainly, but it is the wave's thinnest deliverable. Nothing here is bloat and nothing is wrong; the gap between this and an A is that the wave proved its own law and then broke it three times.
Ledger audit

Clean, and the best this epic has produced. All six slice tasks sit in_progress — not one false 'done' — with every non-merge-gated criterion stamped and carrying quoted run output, all six parented to cloud-console-hardening-epic and linked to this Paper, all six with a live claim. The merge-gated criterion is UNMET on every one, correctly left for the lead (standing law 5). Seven follow-ups were filed published by the builders mid-build: cch-bl-d34-wrapper-list-correction, cch-bl-lifecycle-token-reaper, cch-bl-state-rule-per-declaration-gate, cch-w3-task-birth-attribution, cch-w3-claim-overwrite-fence, cch-bl-smoke-shim-fidelity, cch-bl-reland-check-backtick-trailer. No task outside the wave was touched. Review added one row, cch-bl-source-citation-line-drift, and pulsed all six slice now-lines with the verdict and the branch to merge.
What the lead must know before merging
Merge the -r branches, not the originals — every one carries reviewer fixes. Slice 6 is already on main (#5439); merge only its -r follow-up.
The merge-gated criterion on all six is the LEAD's to close, by MERGE SHA, never a branch SHA (standing law 1 and 5). Slice 6's is closable NOW with e23951203.
Also merge loop-epic/cch-wave-3-review-charter — the wave-log entry, cut clean off origin/main.

Two behaviour changes ride out in the open and are intended, not incidental. HEAD /v1/events now answers 405 instead of opening a stream (D43: no first-party consumer HEADs this console, so this is preventive). And 'blocked' is terminal, so createOrReplace/replace now require an ifRevisionID for it — which makes the create-family doors agree with the patch door.

Sign-out-everywhere now sends { noBounce: true }, so an expired token renders inline in the confirm sheet instead of bouncing to login. That is the confirmModal failure contract and the 2FA-disable precedent, but it IS a change in what a 401 does on that button.

The SSE reaper's first production tick deletes every burned/expired sse row accumulated since #5377 in one unbounded statement. The table is days old so the batch is small, but nobody measured the live row count.
What the next wave takes

This wave paid the class at three doors and NAMED two holes it could not close. The next wave closes the named ones first — that is the sequenced-rounds law applied to residue rather than to files. In order: (1) cch-w3-claim-overwrite-fence, claim theft-by-OVERWRITE, whose first criterion is literally 'MEASURE FIRST' and is unrun — it is the largest remaining hole in the class slice 4 claims to have paid; (2) cch-w3-task-birth-attribution, the forged-fresh-create -> Tasks.Queue.ready hole, the one residual harm this wave measured and left standing; (3) cch-bl-source-citation-line-drift, because three occurrences in one wave is a class, and D41 says a class is paid with a ratchet and not with prose; (4) cch-bl-d34-wrapper-list-correction, because this charter's own D34 does not reproduce its own numbers and a builder had to correct it silently in code to make the census work. cch-bl-smoke-shim-fidelity is the stretch row: the shim's flat registry can still manufacture the D55 false green in a NEW place, and slice 5's fix was discipline, not mechanism.
